description: Ceviche de Camaron is a vibrant and refreshing Mexican seafood dish, featuring fresh shrimp 'cooked' in tangy lime juice. This zesty preparation combines succulent shrimp with crisp vegetables like cucumber, tomato, and onion, all brightened by cilantro and a hint of spice. It is a perfect light meal or appetizer, bursting with authentic Mexican flavors.

ingredients.notes: peeled, deveined, tail off, chopped into 1/2-inch pieces

instructions.title: Prepare the Shrimp
instructions.text: Wash the chopped shrimp thoroughly under cold water and pat them dry with paper towels. Place the shrimp pieces in a non-reactive bowl, such as glass or ceramic.

instructions.title: Marinate the Shrimp
instructions.text: Pour the fresh lime juice over the shrimp, ensuring that all the shrimp pieces are fully submerged in the juice. Stir gently to distribute. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or until the shrimp turn opaque and pink, indicating they are 'cooked' by the acid. Stir occasionally during this process.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: While the shrimp marinates, prepare your vegetables. Finely dice the red onion, cucumber, and tomatoes. Mince the jalapeño if you are using it for a touch of heat. Chop the fresh cilantro.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Once the shrimp has 'cooked' and turned opaque, drain about half of the lime juice from the bowl. Add the diced red onion, cucumber, tomatoes, and minced jalapeño (if using) to the bowl with the shrimp. Mix gently.

instructions.title: Season and Finish
instructions.text: Add the chopped cilantro, salt, and black pepper to taste. Stir all the ingredients together until they are well combined and evenly distributed. Adjust seasonings as needed.

instructions.title: Chill and Serve
instructions.text: Cover the ceviche and refrigerate for another 15-20 minutes to allow all the vibrant flavors to meld together beautifully. Just before serving, gently fold in the diced avocado. Serve immediately with crispy tostadas or your favorite tortilla chips.

tips: For the best flavor and acidity, always use freshly squeezed lime juice. Bottled lime juice will not yield the same vibrant results.

If you are concerned about consuming raw shrimp, you can quickly blanch the shrimp in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until just cooked through, then immediately plunge into an ice bath before marinating in lime juice.
Ceviche is best enjoyed fresh on the day it is made. While it can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 1 day, the texture of the shrimp and vegetables will soften over time.
